summary.text: A bed is a layer of sediment, sedimentary rock or volcanic rock bounded above and below by more or less well-defined bedding surfaces.
Bedding surfaces usually record a change in the rate or type of sediment piling up, such as a pause in deposition, erosion or a shift in flow.
Rules such as superposition, where younger beds lie above older ones unless overturned, let geologists work out the order of events in a rock's history.

items.prompt: A road cut shows three flat, stacked layers of rock that have never been flipped by tectonic forces. Which layer is the oldest?

options.label: The top layer
The middle layer
The bottom layer
They are all the same age

items.explain: By the Law of Superposition, younger rocks are deposited above older ones and stay that way unless the beds are overturned.

items.prompt: On a mountainside you see layers of sedimentary rock standing at a steep slant. What does that most likely mean?

options.label: They were tilted by geologic forces after forming
They were deposited on a steep slope
They formed from lava, not sediment
Each one formed at a different angle

items.explain: By the Law of Original Horizontality, beds are laid down horizontally under gravity, so beds that are not horizontal have been tilted or warped.

items.prompt: A band of igneous rock slices straight up through several layers of sedimentary rock. Which is younger?

options.label: The lowest sedimentary layer
The highest sedimentary layer
They must all be the same age
The igneous rock that slices through

items.explain: By the law of Cross-Cutting Relationships, a feature that cuts through another, such as an igneous dike through bedding, is the younger of the two.

items.prompt: In a normally graded bed, the larger grains sit on the older side. You find a graded bed with its coarse grains on top. What best explains this?

options.label: The grains were sorted by wind
The layer has been overturned
The bed formed very quickly
Larger grains always settle last

items.explain: Normal grading puts larger grains on the older side, which starts at the bottom; coarse grains on top suggest the bed has been flipped, since beds keep their order unless overturned.

items.prompt: Two canyon walls on either side of a river show the same sequence of rock layers. What best explains this?

options.label: The layers were once continuous, then cut by erosion
Two separate seas happened to lay identical layers
The river deposited the same layers on both sides
Earthquakes copied the layers from one side across

items.explain: By the Law of Lateral Continuity, beds extend sideways in all directions, so similar rocks separated by erosion may once have been continuous.

items.prompt: Under the definition that splits layers by thickness, what would you call a coherent sediment layer 3 mm thick?

options.label: A bed
A flow
A lamina
A stratum

items.explain: By the thickness definition, a bed is more than 1 cm thick and a lamina is less than 1 cm thick.
